title: Capture/cursors: slurp snap, shot-only hardware cursors, vmwgfx software cursors
head: bec78e866d7f
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: #12512's visibility filter makes this PR's new capture test fail when both changes merge
leads.consequence: The new Hyprland stub omits visible for every client. #12512 changes the window predicate to .visible == true; all stubbed windows disappear and the first assertion sees the monitor rather than 400,500 400x300. Real Hyprland v0.56.2 includes visible on each client. CI blocks the combined changes until the fixture sets visible:true on the two intended windows (and a separate false case as appropriate). #12512 is diverged from this PR, not stacked; its GitHub mergeable state was MERGEABLE against quattro. A three-way merge of the production script had no markers, so this is a test-contract conflict, not a textual one.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus (run2); published as related-PR note

leads.summary: Refreshing or reinstalling user configs removes the vmwgfx cursor fix
leads.consequence: The workaround exists only as an append to ~/.config/hypr/looknfeel.lua. omarchy-refresh-hyprland copies the shipped looknfeel.lua over it and omarchy-reinstall-configs copies /etc/skel over it; neither reruns the quirk. The shipped config has no no_hardware_cursors setting, Hyprland's default is auto, and on a non-NVIDIA vmwgfx monitor auto does not force software cursors. After config reload/relogin, the VMware user who reset configs can get the invisible pointer again until running user finalization --force or reapplying the setting manually. Consider restoring the hardware quirk after these reset paths or documenting a safe reapply path.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator (bin/omarchy-refresh-hyprland overwrites looknfeel.lua); not published: identical pre-existing behavior for the nouveau quirk this PR copies

leads.summary: #11911 and its stacked successor #11912 conflict on install/user/all.sh
leads.consequence: #11911 adds fix-vmware-scaling.sh at precisely the same insertion point after fix-nouveau-cursor.sh as this PR's fix-vmware-cursor.sh; #11912 includes the #11911 addition. Both are diverged from #12252, while #11912 builds on #11911, so this is one collision with the stacked series, not two independent collisions. Three-way merges yield conflict markers. Merging either series with this PR requires retaining both installer calls or VMware loses one of scaling and software-cursor setup. Both other PRs reported MERGEABLE against current quattro when checked, which does not mean they merge with #12252.

leads.summary: Single-line Lua cursor override remains undetected and is overwritten
leads.consequence: The guard only recognizes a line starting with no_hardware_cursors. A valid `hl.config({ cursor = { no_hardware_cursors = false } })` is not recognized. The script appends a later true assignment and announces forcing software cursors despite the user's explicit false setting. A multiline false control stays unchanged, and a comment-only control correctly gets an assignment. Match a non-comment assignment anywhere on its line or otherwise parse config safely before appending.
leads.triage: same as prior F4, corroborates Opus; published

leads.summary: Equal-area candidate picks do not match slurp v1.5.0's highlight
leads.consequence: slurp's comparator skips only when the current selection has strictly less area than the next. Equal-size overlapping rectangles therefore select the LAST candidate. resolve_rect_at instead replaces only on strictly smaller area, retaining the FIRST. On a bare click the saved recording region can differ from the highlighted rectangle; keyboard selection probes also use this helper. Use <= and update the line 65 comment.
leads.triage: same as prior F3, corroborates Opus; published

leads.summary: Existing VMware installs do not receive the new cursor quirk during upgrade
leads.consequence: The new call is only reached by user finalization. That step exits on its finalize-user marker, while normal upgrades run pending files under migrations/ and the PR adds none. Existing VMware users who need software cursors will not get the fix until manual --force finalization or a migration. A migration calling the quirk after config has been seeded would cover them.
leads.triage: same as prior migration note, corroborates Opus; published

leads.summary: Non-ISO installs can lack lspci and silently miss the vmwgfx repair
leads.consequence: The ISO's base list includes inxi, which depends on pciutils, so this does not affect a stock ISO. But the runtime omarchy PKGBUILD deliberately has minimal hard dependencies and does not depend on pciutils/inxi. On a package-only or customized VMware installation with no lspci, omarchy-cmd-present returns 1 and user finalization records success without a visible cursor warning or workaround. Either ensure the detector's dependency exists for that supported installation route, use a sysfs fallback, or surface the skipped repair.
leads.triage: factual, not independently verified beyond seeing the same omarchy-cmd-present lspci guard in fix-nouveau-cursor.sh; not published: pre-existing shared pattern, low value

leads.summary: vmware test passes with a wrong lspci argument
leads.consequence: Its lspci stub unconditionally prints `Kernel driver in use` even if the script drops -k. Real lspci in terse mode prints this line only with -k (or verbose mode), so the mutant would skip the cursor repair in production. The mutated script nevertheless passes every vmware test. Assert the stub receives `-k` and supply a negative control with no -k.
leads.triage: test-fidelity lead (stub ignores argv); not published: same stub pattern as nouveau test, low value

leads.summary: capture test does not distinguish the slurp tie bug from the corrected comparator
leads.consequence: The fixed rectangles have different areas, so this test passes both with today's wrong strict < and with the slurp-matching <= comparator; the current broken `<` comparator and a corrected `<=` variant both pass every assertion. Add overlapping equal-area distinct rectangles and assert the last in stdin order is chosen, including the --select-window path if this shared helper stays in that path.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus (<= mutant passes PR test); folded into F3 suggested change

leads.summary: Capture helper comment and PR title/description still describe screenshot behavior absent from this head
leads.consequence: The new click-snap helper is exercised by built-in screen recording, not the screenshot command: omarchy-capture-screenshot execs Omasnap. The current diff has no screenshot changes, yet the PR title and Summary still promise shot-only hardware cursors. This is not a new screenshot regression, since Omasnap has its own click behavior. Update the helper's introductory comment and the PR title/description to reflect the new scope.
leads.triage: PR title/summary part corroborates Opus and is published; comment at bin/omarchy-capture-region:7-9 is pre-existing text outside the diff, not published

limits: The visual premise that every VMware vmwgfx configuration fails to display the hardware cursor was not settled by source alone; a live guest with both 3D modes or a vendor-specific reproduction would settle hardware behavior. Do not treat this as verified.

The current external omarchy-pkgs checkout is packaged v4.0.4, not this future PR head. Its package recipe globbed bin/ and copied the entire install/ tree, but whether the PR is released with a changed recipe depends on a future package build.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12252#issuecomment-5834887325) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12252#issuecomment-5835061826), checked at `bec78e8`.

**Verified:** the rebase drops only the screenshot cursor commit, as the reply says. The two remaining commits carry the same patches as before, and all five changed files are byte-identical to the previously reviewed head. The earlier Verified results still hold on this head and on a local merge into current `quattro` (`3faafba`): both new tests pass, and both fail when copied onto `d201fb9` or `3faafba` without the PR's changes.

| Earlier point | Status at `bec78e8` |
|---|---|
| Screenshot hunk has no target on `quattro` | Resolved: hunk and `screenshot-cursor-test.sh` removed |
| Hardware-cursor switch after the pick | No longer applies: that code is gone |
| Bare-click tie-break differs from slurp | Still present (see below) |
| vmwgfx guard misses a one-line setting | Still present, unchanged |
| Existing installs need a migration | Still applies, no migration added |

### Bare-click tie-break still differs from slurp's highlight

The message of `f4c72a6` says `resolve_rect_at` "keeps the first on a tie, the way slurp's own highlight and geo_at_cursor do". That holds for `geo_at_cursor`, which calls `resolve_rect_at` itself. It does not hold for slurp v1.5.0: `add_choice_box` appends boxes in input order, and `seat_update_selection` replaces the highlighted box unless it is strictly smaller, so the last equal-area box wins. The retained comment above `resolve_rect_at` makes the same claim.

slurp's selection functions, copied verbatim into a small harness, were fed the same candidate list the script gives slurp:

```text
candidates: 0,0 2560x1440 | 400,500 400x300 | 500,550 400x300    point 600,600
  slurp v1.5.0 selection code:     500,550 400x300
  resolve_rect_at (head, <):       400,500 400x300
  resolve_rect_at with <=:         500,550 400x300
```

**Impact:** limited to overlapping candidates of equal area, such as two same-size floating windows. A bare click inside the overlap then selects a different window from the one highlighted (screen recording is the caller that uses this mode). The PR newly routes bare clicks through this rule. `--take-window` has the same mismatch; it already did before the PR.

**Suggested change:** use `((area <= smallest_area))`, and change the comment (and commit message) to "last on a tie". The new `capture-region-test.sh` passes with either comparator, so a case with two overlapping equal-area windows would lock this in.

### vmwgfx guard still overrides a one-line explicit setting

Unchanged from the earlier review: with `hl.config({ cursor = { no_hardware_cursors = false } })` on one line, the quirk still appends its `true` block after it. A multi-line assignment is still respected. Both cases were rerun on this head.

**Impact:** on a vmwgfx install where the user explicitly set `no_hardware_cursors = false` on one line, the appended block overrides that choice.

**Suggested change:** match `no_hardware_cursors[[:space:]]*=` anywhere on a non-comment line.

**Migration note:** still applies. The quirk runs only from `install/user/all.sh`, and source reading shows `bin/omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro` does not source that file either, so neither existing installs nor upgraded ones get it automatically without a migration. The nouveau quirk has the same gap.

**PR description:** the title ("shot-only hardware cursors") and summary ("hardware cursors only for the shot") still describe the screenshot cursor change, which is no longer part of this PR.

**Related open PRs:**
- #12512 filters windows on `.visible == true`. With both merged, `capture-region-test.sh` fails (`actual: 0,0 2560x1440`) because its stub clients have no `visible` key. Adding `"hidden":false,"visible":true` to the two stub clients, as real `hyprctl clients -j` output includes, keeps it passing under either filter.
- #11911 (and #11912, which contains it) inserts a line at the same spot in `install/user/all.sh`, so one of them needs a trivial conflict resolution that keeps both lines.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the new head, the previous head, the merge base and current `quattro`, plus slurp v1.5.0 and Hyprland v0.56.2 source. Both new tests ran in a sandbox with every backend stubbed, on the head, on a local merge into `quattro`, and on base trees as negative controls. The tie case ran slurp's own selection code in a harness, not slurp under a compositor. Related PRs were checked by local merges; the #12512 interaction was run. No live desktop, VMware guest or real capture was tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
